Title: I Built an AI Content Agent With N8N and Claude (Step-by-Step)

Author: Greg Isenberg

Thumbnail: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/m9iaJNJE2-M/hqdefault.jpg

Description:
Join me as chat I with The Boring Marketer as we demonstrate a complete n8n workflow automation that can save content creators 10-15 hours weekly by scraping top-performing content, generating new content ideas, and publishing to social. The system uses N8N to orchestrate multiple AI tools that research, write, and even create images for posts, with an optional human review step before publishing.

Build an AI Content Automation in n8n: https://www.gregisenberg.com/ai-content-automation

Get ideas, tools, and tactics to 10x your marketing: https://www.skool.com/the-vibe-marketers

Timestamps:

00:00 - Intro
01:58 - Why use this Content AI Agent
03:05 - Demoing the n8n workflow
03:33 - Explanation workflow stages
04:52 - Appify for content scraping
05:57 - Researching Viral Content
06:59 - Content curation and Idea generation
11:47 - Overview of OpenRouter for accessing multiple LLMs
13:23 - Claude 3.7 Sonnet for content creation
14:23 - Prompting Tips
18:05 - Demo of the human review/posting process
22:33 - Get free workflow template

Key Points:

• The workflow uses N8N to automate content creation by scraping top-performing content from YouTube and X (Twitter)
• The system processes this data through various LLMs (including Claude and OpenAI) to generate original content ideas
• The workflow can automatically create and publish LinkedIn posts with minimal human intervention
• Tools mentioned include Appify (for scraping), OpenRouter (for accessing multiple LLMs), and Claude 3.7 Sonnet (for writing)

1) THE PROBLEM:

Creating quality content across multiple platforms is EXHAUSTING.

Most marketers waste hours researching, writing, and publishing���only to get mediocre results.

What if AI could do the heavy lifting while you focus on strategy?

That's exactly what this workflow solves!

2) THE WORKFLOW OVERVIEW:

This N8n automation has 4 key stages:
• Data collection from YouTube \u0026 X
• Content idea generation
• Research \u0026 validation
• Content creation \u0026 publishing

All with minimal human input! Let's dive deeper...

3) STAGE 1: DATA COLLECTION 

The workflow uses Appify to:
• Scrape top-performing YouTube videos on your topic
• Transcribe video content automatically
• Pull relevant tweets from X
• Compile everything into one massive data block

This gives your AI REAL context about what's working!

4) STAGE 2: IDEA GENERATION 

Once you have the data, the workflow:
• Feeds everything to an OpenAI LLM
• Analyzes patterns in high-performing content
• Generates fresh angles and hooks
• Identifies optimal content formats

No more staring at blank screens wondering what to write!

5) STAGE 3: RESEARCH \u0026 VALIDATION 

This is where it gets POWERFUL:
• Uses Perplexity (via OpenRouter) to find facts \u0026 stats
• Validates content ideas with real-world data
• Prevents AI hallucinations
• Adds credibility to your content

Your posts will be backed by ACTUAL research!

6) STAGE 4: CONTENT CREATION 

The workflow uses Claude 3.7 Sonnet (the BEST writing AI right now) to:
• Create a complete LinkedIn post
• Generate an accompanying image
• Format everything properly
• Send to you for approval via Slack

One click and it's published!

7) PRO TIPS FROM @boringmarketer:

• Give AI specific brand voice instructions
• Tell it to avoid corporate jargon and fluff
• Ban those AI-looking dashes (---)
• Mention \

Title: n8n vs Make.com AI Agents: Which One Is Better?

Author: The AI Automators

Thumbnail: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/C7hYdp9VlnY/hqdefault.jpg

Description:
👉 Get all of our blueprints and learn how to customize them https://www.theaiautomators.com/?utm_source=youtube\u0026utm_medium=video\u0026utm_campaign=tutorial\u0026utm_content=n8nvsmake

In this video, I compare the brand new (beta) AI Agent system from Make.com against the more established AI Agents in N8N. 

Choosing the right platform is crucial for building powerful AI automations, so I break down the key differences side-by-side across numerous categories to help you decide which system best suits your needs. 

l explore everything from setup and usability to advanced features like RAG and multi-agent capabilities.

I evaluate them across key areas including:

User Experience (UX) \u0026 Ease of Setup
Interfaces \u0026 Triggers (including Chatbots)
LLM Support \u0026 Reasoning Capabilities
Tool Integration \u0026 Flexibility
Memory \u0026 Session Handling
Knowledge Retrieval (RAG) Functionality
Structured Output Formats
Debugging \u0026 Error Handling
Deployment Options \u0026 Privacy
Pricing \u0026 Value
And more!
Whether you're a Make.com power user exploring their new AI features, an N8N automation pro, or just deciding which platform to learn for AI agents, you'll get a clear, unbiased comparison of their strengths and weaknesses right now.

🔗 Related Links:
Make.com: https://www.make.com/
N8N: https://n8n.io/
Our N8N Multi-Agent HAL 9001 Video: https://youtu.be/7mmJYk5b59U?si=kcWJ5IPQCQ858mC-

Title: I Built My Claude Code Subagents DREAM TEAM to Create Any AI Agent

Author: Cole Medin

Thumbnail: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/HJ9VvIG3Rps/hqdefault.jpg

Description:
Here's how I used Claude Code subagents along with Archon to build my dream team of agentic coders to create any AI Agent. This template is available for you to try right now - link below!

You just have to describe at a high level the agent you want to create, and then Claude Code spins up an entire workflow to plan, create, and validate the agent.

The highly structured approach to defining and executing subagents in Claude Code is a thing of beauty. And with Archon, we can give them the knowledge they need and split tasks for our project between them. This, my friend, is next level agentic engineering.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

- Check out Lindy if you want to easily build AI automations with no code that scale *unbelievably* well:
https://go.lindy.ai/cole-med

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

- If you're looking to join a community for early AI adopters all mastering AI coding and sharing goldmines of resources with each other, check out Dynamous:
https://dynamous.ai

- GitHub repo for this subagent dream team:
https://github.com/coleam00/context-engineering-intro/tree/main/use-cases/agent-factory-with-subagents

- Try Archon now (free and open source):
https://archon.diy

- Archon intro video:
https://youtu.be/8pRc_s2VQIo

- Links to crawl with Archon for this template:
Claude Code: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/sub-agents
Pydantic AI: https://ai.pydantic.dev/llms-full.txt
